name: Hospital Bag Checklist
description: Everything to pack for labor, delivery, and your first days postpartum.

items.text: Pack your photo ID and insurance card in an outside pocket
Bring your hospital pre-registration or admission paperwork
Add a copy of your birth plan, with a few extra printouts
Include your prenatal records or your provider's contact information
items.note: Ask your provider whether you need to bring records or if they share them directly.

items.text: Pack your phone and a long charging cable
Bring a small amount of cash for vending machines or parking
Pack a comfortable robe and warm socks with grip soles
Bring two or three pairs of high-waisted, breathable underwear
Add a loose going-home outfit that fits a postpartum body
Pack two nursing bras or comfortable soft bras
Include lip balm, hair ties, and a wide-tooth comb
Bring your eyeglasses and contact lens supplies if you wear them
Add flip-flops for the shower
Pack a few favorite snacks for after delivery
items.note: Check with your provider about eating during labor itself.

items.text: Bring a refillable water bottle with a straw
Add a small fan or handheld mister for warmth and cooling
Include a playlist, earbuds, or a portable speaker
Pack a focal item or photo that helps you relax
Bring an extra pillow from home with a colored pillowcase
Pack a toothbrush, toothpaste, and travel-size deodorant
Bring a gentle face wash and your everyday moisturizer
Add dry shampoo and a small hairbrush
Include any prescription medications in their original bottles
Pack overnight pads and disposable underwear for postpartum bleeding
Bring nipple cream if you plan to breastfeed
Pack a full change of clothes and comfortable shoes
Bring a separate phone charger and a battery pack
Add snacks and a refillable water bottle
Include a small toiletry kit and a light blanket
Pack a sweater or hoodie, since hospital rooms run cold
Install the car seat in advance and learn how to buckle it
Pack two newborn outfits plus a soft going-home outfit
Bring a hat, socks, and scratch mittens
Add a weather-appropriate bunting or blanket for the ride home
Include a swaddle blanket if you have a favorite
Pack any pacifiers you'd like to try, if you choose to use them
Confirm the route to the hospital and a backup route
Top off the car's gas tank ahead of your due date
Set out a list of emergency contacts and your provider's number
Arrange pet or older-sibling care and have it on standby
Charge your phone and camera the night before if labor signs appear

faq.q: When should I pack my hospital bag?
faq.a: Aim to have your bag ready by around 36 weeks, since babies can arrive earlier than planned. Packing early means everything is set if labor starts unexpectedly. Keep the finished bag near the door or in your car so you can grab it quickly when the time comes.

faq.q: What should I not bring to the hospital?
faq.a: Skip valuables like expensive jewelry and large amounts of cash. You usually don't need to pack diapers, wipes, or formula, since the hospital provides these. Leave bulky pillows at home unless you really want your own, and avoid overpacking clothes you won't realistically use.

faq.q: How many outfits should I pack for the baby?
faq.a: Pack two or three newborn outfits plus a going-home outfit. Bring different sizes if you can, since newborn size may run small or large depending on your baby. Include socks and a hat. The hospital supplies blankets and diapers, so you can pack light here.

faq.q: Do I need to bring my own toiletries?
faq.a: Yes, bring your own toiletries for comfort. Hospitals offer basics, but your own toothbrush, lip balm, hair ties, and a gentle face wash make recovery feel more like home. Travel sizes work well. Add glasses or contact supplies if you wear them, since you may not want lenses during labor.

faq.q: Should my partner pack a separate bag?
faq.a: A small separate bag for your partner helps a lot. Include a change of clothes, snacks, a phone charger, and toiletries. Your partner may stay overnight, so comfortable clothes and something to do during quieter moments make the experience easier for both of you.
